Deep static trace of auth/session enforcement and public API exposure

data.reason: Critical REST API endpoints are exposed without authentication/authorization checks (no SessionAuth/require_auth dependency).

poc.description: Unauthenticated call to /api/agents (and related routers) to create/start agents, clone repos, read files, and invoke chat using server-side provider keys.

data.impact: Unauthenticated remote control of the auditing service: create/start/cancel agents, clone/delete repos, browse repo files, fetch findings and LLM interaction logs, and trigger LLM calls using API keys stored in server settings.
data.evidence_snippet:
backend/routers/agents.py (unauthenticated handler)
router = APIRouter()

@router.post("", response_model=Agent)
async def create_agent(request: AgentCreateRequest):
    agent = await orchestrator.create_agent(request)
    return agent
source_to_sink_path: services/agent_orchestrator.py#AgentOrchestrator.create_agent (instantiates agent; may load provider API key from settings)
agents/* Agent.run() executes audits; results exposed via /api/agents/* and /ws
data.fix_plan: Require authentication on all non-health endpoints by default (e.g., add Depends(require_auth) to routers in backend/main.py or per-router), and make any bootstrap token retrieval non-network-exposed (stdout on startup / localhost-only) or replace with proper user auth.
data.regression_test_plan: Add FastAPI TestClient tests asserting 401 for representative endpoints (e.g., POST /api/agents, POST /api/git/clone, GET /api/files/{id}/tree, POST /api/chat) when no token is provided, and 200 only when a valid token is supplied.

variants.disposition: validated (unauthenticated; uses stored provider API keys)
hardening (token required, but token can be fetched via /api/auth/token)

data.reason: The master session token is disclosed via an unauthenticated HTTP endpoint, defeating the session guard used on /api/settings and /ws.

poc.description: GET /api/auth/token returns the master token; reuse as X-Session-Token or ?token= to access protected endpoints (/api/settings/*) and /ws.

data.impact: Authentication bypass for the settings API and WebSocket channel: remote callers can obtain a valid session token and perform any settings operations (including changing provider configuration).
source_to_sink_path: backend/routers/settings.py protected endpoints accept X-Session-Token/?token (now attacker-controlled)

validators.name: SessionAuth(require_auth)
validators.disposition: not applied to /api/auth/token (missing auth for bootstrap)

data.fix_plan: Remove the network-exposed token bootstrap endpoint. Safer defaults: print the token to server logs on startup for local use, bind auth bootstrap to localhost only, or replace with real user auth (OIDC/JWT) before exposing beyond localhost.
data.regression_test_plan: Test that /api/auth/token is not remotely accessible by default (or requires auth), and that /api/settings/* rejects requests without a valid token obtained via an authenticated flow.

variants.disposition: hardening (allows ?token= query param which is easy to leak)
validated chain (token reuse grants WS access)

Session token persists to disk without explicit permission hardening; default umask may allow broader reads in some deployments.
data.suggestion: Write token file with 0600 permissions (or store in a proper secrets manager) and avoid exposing it via bind-mounted volumes.

data.reason: Session token accepted via query param (?token=) can be leaked via logs, proxies, and referrers; prefer header-only transport.
data.suggestion: Remove query-param token support and require X-Session-Token header (or cookies with SameSite+CSRF for browser flows).

data.reason: Path traversal guard in file_service uses string prefix check (startswith) on resolved paths; prefix-collision can allow sibling-path escape if future auth/tenancy is added.
data.suggestion: Use Path.is_relative_to(repo_root) (Py>=3.9) or os.path.commonpath to enforce directory containment, not string prefix.

data.reason: POST /api/auth/session issues a fresh valid session token without any prior authentication, enabling access to endpoints protected by SessionAuth.

data.note: Fix for token bypass must cover BOTH /api/auth/token and /api/auth/session (and any other unauthenticated token minting).
